name: Cross-book consensus divergence on player_assists
thesis: When the devigged consensus fair probability from 3+ books diverges from the target book's implied by 2%+, the consensus is correct more often than the target book. This is the core model.

name: Cross-book consensus divergence on player_rebounds
thesis: When the devigged consensus fair probability from 3+ books diverges from the target book's implied by 2%+, the consensus is correct more often than the target book. This is the core model.

name: Divisional underdog spread value
thesis: Divisional underdogs in the NFL cover at a significantly higher rate than non-divisional underdogs because familiarity compresses talent gaps. Books overprice favorites in divisional matchups because public money inflates lines on the better team. Divisional dogs of 3-10 points cover at 53%+ ATS historically, with the edge strongest in the second meeting of the season when game-planning advantages compound.

name: NFL West Coast team early kickoff spread fade
thesis: West Coast (Pacific time zone) teams playing 1pm ET road games (10am body clock) underperform the spread by 1-2 points, particularly in weeks 1-8 before bodies adapt to travel rhythms. Books partially price this but underweight it for non-marquee matchups — fading the West Coast road team in early kickoffs yields >54% ATS.

name: NFL altitude QB passing props
thesis: Visiting QBs playing at Denver (5,280 ft) show measurably lower completion rates and higher interception rates due to ball flight physics and reduced oxygen. Books price passing yards props based on season averages without sufficient altitude discount, creating under value on visiting QB passing yards at Mile High.

name: NFL bye week rust spreads
thesis: Teams returning from bye weeks are overvalued by the market. The 'rest advantage' narrative inflates public confidence and compresses spreads toward the bye team. Historical data shows bye-week teams cover at below 50% against divisional opponents and road games, where rust outweighs rest. Fading bye teams in these spots yields persistent closing line value.

name: NFL divisional revenge spread compression
thesis: In the second divisional matchup of the season, teams that lost the first meeting by 10+ points as underdogs cover the spread at >56% in the rematch. Scheme familiarity and motivational revenge factor compress blowout margins, but books anchor partially on the first-meeting result, inflating the spread for the rematch favorite.

name: NFL divisional revenge spread overreaction
thesis: In divisional rematches where the first meeting was decided by 14+ points, public money overweights the blowout result and inflates the spread for the rematch. Divisional familiarity and coaching adjustments compress margins in rematches, creating value on the dog in the second meeting.

name: NFL dome-to-outdoor total deflation
thesis: When a dome team (e.g., Falcons, Cowboys, Lions, Colts, Cardinals, Raiders, Texans, Saints, Vikings, Rams, Chargers, Commanders, Bills) travels to an outdoor cold-weather venue (temp < 40°F or wind > 15 mph), game totals close lower than the opener by 1.5+ points but books undershoot the adjustment — the under still hits at >55% rate, creating persistent under value on these totals.

name: NFL early line movement CLV capture
thesis: NFL spreads that move 1.5+ points between opening (Sunday night) and Wednesday see the move continue toward closing in the same direction 60%+ of the time, as early sharp money signals information the market hasn't fully absorbed. Betting the direction of early movement at the Wednesday number captures closing line value before public money arrives Thursday-Sunday.

name: NFL referee crew total bias
thesis: Specific NFL referee crews show persistent over/under tendencies (penalty yards allowed, pace of play impact) that deviate >2 points from the posted total. When a high-flag crew (top quartile in penalties/game historically) is assigned, overs hit at >54% because books don't adjust totals for crew assignment, which is announced Tuesday/Wednesday — giving a 2-4 day edge window before line movement absorbs it.

name: NFL short-week road underdog spread value
thesis: Road underdogs of 3-7 points on Thursday Night Football or any short-week game (<=5 days rest) where the home team also played the previous Monday/Sunday cover at a rate >53% ATS. Books overweight home advantage on short rest without fully accounting for reduced preparation parity — both teams are equally impaired, but the line inflates the home side.

name: NFL short-week travel totals
thesis: Teams playing on short rest (Thursday Night Football, or <6 days rest) after traveling 1000+ miles show depressed offensive efficiency. Books underadjust totals for the compounding fatigue of short rest + long travel, creating consistent under value on game totals when both factors coincide.

name: Post-bye favorite overpricing
thesis: NFL teams coming off bye weeks are overvalued by the public as favorites. The market narrative that extra preparation time benefits the better team creates inflated lines. Teams favored by 4+ points after a bye cover at only 46-48% historically because the line already prices in the bye advantage plus an additional public premium. Fading post-bye favorites of 4+ points yields consistent ATS value.

name: Referee crew total bias
thesis: NFL referee crews show persistent, measurable bias in penalty frequency and type that affects game totals. High-flag crews (top quartile in penalties called per game) inflate scoring through extended drives and free yardage, while low-flag crews suppress it. Books set totals based on team matchups but do not adjust for assigned referee crew tendencies. Games officiated by top-quartile flag crews see 3+ more total points on average, creating systematic over value.

name: Short-week Thursday total unders
thesis: NFL teams playing on Thursday Night Football after a Sunday game show reduced offensive efficiency due to compressed preparation and recovery windows. Totals for Thursday games are systematically set too high because books anchor to full-rest scoring averages. Teams with fewer than 4 days rest score 2-3 fewer points per game on average, creating persistent under value on game totals.

name: Weather impact on MLB totals
thesis: Games played in high wind conditions see reduced scoring. Books don't fully adjust totals for weather — Under is +EV when wind_mph exceeds 15.

name: Weather impact on NFL totals
thesis: Games played in high wind conditions see reduced scoring. Books don't fully adjust totals for weather — Under is +EV when wind_mph exceeds 15.

name: West-to-East early kickoff spread fade
thesis: West Coast NFL teams traveling east for 1pm ET kickoffs (10am body clock) underperform the spread due to circadian disadvantage. This effect is strongest in weeks 1-8 before teams adapt travel routines, and compounds when the traveling team played a late Sunday/Monday game the prior week. Books underweight travel direction and kickoff timing, creating 1.5-2 point spread mispricing on the visiting West Coast team.

name: nfl_altitude_totals_denver
thesis: Game totals for Denver home games are underpriced by 1.5-2.5 points. Altitude at 5,280 feet reduces air density, increasing passing distance and kick distance while accelerating fatigue in visiting teams' defensive lines by the 4th quarter. The effect is strongest in September/October when visiting teams have not acclimated and temperature differentials between departure city and Denver are largest. Books partially price altitude but underweight the fatigue-driven 4th quarter scoring surge.

name: nfl_altitude_visitor_total_fade
thesis: Visiting teams at Denver (5,280ft) underperform their team total in early-season games (weeks 1-8) by 1.5-2.5 points when they are not a mountain-region team and have not played at altitude in the prior 3 weeks. Reduced oxygen capacity degrades pass rush, WR route crispness, and kicking accuracy. Books price Denver's home advantage into the spread but underadjust visitor team totals specifically. The effect diminishes in cold-weather late season when all teams face environmental stress.

name: nfl_bye_week_bounce_totals
thesis: Teams returning from bye weeks are systematically under-totaled in their first game back. Rest advantage leads to sharper offensive execution, but books anchor to pre-bye scoring averages which often included fatigued late-season performances. The edge is strongest when both teams are coming off byes (rare) or when a rested team faces a team on a short week.

name: nfl_bye_week_bounce_totals
thesis: Teams returning from bye weeks show inflated offensive performance in their first game back, as extra preparation time disproportionately benefits offensive scheming. Books underadjust game totals for post-bye teams, creating value on overs in the first half especially. Test by comparing actual totals vs closing line for post-bye games across 3+ seasons.

name: nfl_bye_week_bounce_totals
thesis: Teams returning from bye weeks show inflated offensive efficiency in their first game back, but books under-adjust totals. The extra preparation time correlates with higher-scoring first halves, creating value on game totals when both or one team is off a bye.

name: nfl_bye_week_return_unders
thesis: Teams returning from bye weeks are overvalued by the public due to perceived rest advantage, inflating spreads and totals. Books adjust lines toward the popular side, creating value on unders and against-the-spread for opponents. The rest advantage is already priced in but public money pushes it further, especially in prime-time slots where casual bettors dominate.

name: nfl_bye_week_rust_totals
thesis: Teams returning from bye weeks show inflated totals in their first game back, as books overweight rest advantage while underpricing offensive rust and timing disruption. The under hits at a higher rate in bye-return games, especially when the total is set above the season average for both teams.

name: nfl_bye_week_rust_unders
thesis: Teams returning from bye weeks in the NFL show a tendency toward lower-scoring first halves due to scheme rust and timing disruption, particularly when facing opponents that played the previous week. The market overvalues the 'rest advantage' narrative and prices totals too high for these matchups. First-half unders and game unders should show +EV when the consensus devig line implies less than 3% edge on the under.

name: nfl_bye_week_under_returning
thesis: Teams returning from bye weeks are overvalued by the public, leading to inflated spreads. Books adjust totals but the spread market lags because casual bettors assume rest = dominance. In reality, teams coming off byes since 2020 have covered at ~47% against the spread, creating a fade opportunity especially when they are favored by 3+ points.

name: nfl_cold_weather_total_under_dome_teams
thesis: When a dome/warm-weather home team (ATL, ARI, DAL, HOU, IND, JAX, LAC, LAR, LV, MIA, NO, TB) plays an outdoor road game in sub-40°F conditions, the game total under hits at 58%+. Players accustomed to climate-controlled environments show measurable grip and route-running degradation. Edge is highest when the temperature delta between home stadium norm and game-day conditions exceeds 35°F and wind speed is above 10mph.

name: nfl_cold_weather_under_dome_qb
thesis: When a quarterback who plays home games in a dome or warm climate starts an outdoor game with kickoff temperature below 35°F, the game total under hits at an elevated rate. Grip, ball aerodynamics, and timing route precision degrade for cold-unadjusted passers, compressing both teams' offensive output. Books underweight the interaction between QB home-venue type and game-day temperature, especially in December and January.

name: nfl_cold_weather_under_dome_teams
thesis: When dome-based or warm-climate NFL teams (ATL, ARI, DAL, LV, LAR, LAC, NO, MIA, JAX, TB) play outdoor road games with kickoff temperature below 35°F, the game total goes under at a 58-62% rate. Books adjust totals for weather but underestimate the compounding effect on passing efficiency when skill players are unaccustomed to cold. The edge increases with wind speed above 10mph.

name: nfl_cross_country_travel_dog_cover
thesis: When a West Coast team travels to an East Coast venue for a 1pm ET kickoff, the away team underperforms relative to the line due to circadian disadvantage (effectively an 10am body-clock start). The home team covers at ~55%. The effect is strongest for road favorites — the market trusts the better team but doesn't price the travel/time-zone cost, creating value on the home dog.

name: nfl_cross_country_travel_dog_spread
thesis: Road underdogs traveling cross-country (2+ time zones) in early kickoff slots (1pm ET) underperform ATS at a lower rate than the market implies. Books overadjust for the travel narrative on marquee matchups, creating value on the traveling dog when the line moves past the key number. Focus on West Coast teams playing 1pm ET East Coast games where the spread has widened 1+ points from open.

name: nfl_cross_country_travel_spread
thesis: West coast teams traveling to early 1pm ET east coast games underperform the spread by 1.5-2.5 points due to circadian disadvantage. This effect is amplified in cold-weather outdoor stadiums and following a short week (Thursday or Monday prior game).

name: nfl_divisional_dog_ats
thesis: Divisional underdogs of 3-7 points cover at a significantly higher rate than non-divisional underdogs at the same spread range. Familiarity breeds closer games — scheme awareness, personnel knowledge, and rivalry motivation compress margins. Books underadjust the divisional familiarity factor in mid-range spreads.

name: nfl_divisional_dog_ats
thesis: Divisional underdogs of 3-7 points cover at a significantly higher rate than implied by market pricing, particularly in the second meeting of the season. Familiarity compresses talent gaps — scheme adjustments from film study disproportionately benefit the weaker team. Books overprice the favorite due to public bias toward the better record.

name: nfl_divisional_dog_ats_late_season
thesis: Divisional underdogs of 3-7 points in weeks 12-18 cover at a rate exceeding implied probability by 4-6%, driven by familiarity asymmetry: inferior rosters know the opponent's scheme intimately and play motivated (rivalry + playoff spoiler). Public money inflates favorites in marquee divisional spots, pushing lines past true value. The edge is strongest when the dog won the first meeting or lost by ≤3.

name: nfl_divisional_dog_ats_late_season
thesis: Divisional underdogs of 3-7 points in weeks 12-18 cover at a significantly higher rate than implied by market price. Familiarity effect compresses true talent gap in divisional rematches — defensive coordinators have film from the first meeting, and scheme adjustments disproportionately help the weaker team. Books overprice the favorite due to recency bias from the first meeting result. Historical ATS rate for this filter should exceed 54% against the spread.

name: nfl_divisional_dog_clv
thesis: Divisional underdogs of 3-7 points exhibit positive closing line value at a significantly higher rate than non-divisional underdogs at the same spread range. Familiarity compresses talent gaps in division games, but opening lines are set off power ratings that don't fully discount scheme familiarity and rivalry motivation. Backing divisional dogs at open yields 2-4% CLV on average, indicating persistent market inefficiency in this subset.

name: nfl_divisional_rematch_under
thesis: The second regular-season meeting between divisional opponents hits the under at a rate exceeding market-implied probability. Defensive coordinators have recent film and scheme familiarity, compressing scoring variance. Books anchor totals to season averages rather than adjusting for schematic convergence in rematches.

name: nfl_divisional_rematch_under
thesis: In the second divisional meeting of the season, the under hits at a significantly higher rate than implied. Defensive coordinators have a full extra game film of the opponent's scheme, leading to better coverage and pressure packages. Books anchor totals partly on the first meeting's score, failing to price the defensive adjustment effect. Edge is strongest when the first meeting was high-scoring (combined 50+).

name: nfl_divisional_revenge_dog_ats
thesis: In the second divisional meeting of the season, teams that lost the first matchup by 10+ points cover the spread at a rate above 55% when getting 3+ points. Coaching staffs have film-specific adjustments, motivational narrative advantage, and books overprice the blowout recency bias. Effect is amplified when the revenge team is at home for the second meeting.

name: nfl_divisional_revenge_over
thesis: NFL divisional rematches where the losing team from the first meeting is now at home show inflated total scoring. Familiarity breeds offensive adjustment — defensive schemes seen once are partially decoded, and coaching staffs game-plan aggressively to avenge the loss. Overs in divisional revenge home games hit at a higher rate than the market implies, especially when the first meeting was decided by 7+ points.

name: nfl_divisional_revenge_unders
thesis: Second divisional matchups of the season where the losing team from the first meeting is now at home trend under the total. Familiarity breeds defensive adjustment — the revenge team game-plans conservatively to avoid another loss, and the winner from game 1 plays tighter expecting a tougher contest. Under hits at 56%+ in these spots historically, with the edge strongest when the first meeting was decided by 7+ points.

name: nfl_divisional_under_late_season
thesis: NFL divisional games in weeks 12-18 trend under the posted total at a significantly higher rate than non-divisional games. Defensive familiarity compounds over the season as coordinators have film from the first matchup. Books set totals based on season-long offensive output rather than adjusting for the second-meeting defensive schematic advantage. The edge is strongest when both teams have winning records.

name: nfl_divisional_under_late_season
thesis: Divisional rivalry games in weeks 12-18 trend under the total at a 56%+ rate because defensive coordinators have full film packages on familiar offenses, and both teams play more conservatively with playoff implications. Books weight recent offensive output too heavily.

name: nfl_divisional_under_late_season
thesis: Divisional games in weeks 12-18 go under the posted total at a significantly higher rate (~56%) than non-divisional games. Defensive familiarity compounds over the season as coordinators have fresh film from the first matchup. Books don't sufficiently discount totals for second divisional meetings, especially when the first meeting was low-scoring.

name: nfl_divisional_under_late_season
thesis: NFL divisional rematches in weeks 14-18 trend under the total at a statistically significant rate. Defensive coordinators have full film from the first matchup, leading to more conservative offensive playcalling and tighter defensive schemes. Books anchor totals to season-long offensive averages rather than adjusting for the familiarity discount in the second divisional meeting.

name: nfl_divisional_underdog_late_season
thesis: Divisional underdogs of 3-7 points in weeks 14-18 cover at a rate exceeding implied probability by 4-6%. Late-season divisional games feature scheme familiarity that compresses talent gaps, and desperate teams with playoff implications play above their season baseline. Books overprice the favorite based on full-season metrics that don't capture the divisional familiarity effect or situational motivation asymmetry.

name: nfl_high_altitude_visitor_fourth_quarter
thesis: Visiting teams playing in Denver underperform fourth-quarter spreads and player rushing prop overs hit at reduced rates (52-55% under rate) due to altitude-induced fatigue manifesting late in games. Books price full-game lines with a small Denver home-field bump but don't adequately adjust live or prop markets for the nonlinear fatigue curve. The effect is strongest for teams from sea-level cities and in September when altitude adaptation is zero.

name: nfl_home_underdog_moneyline_value
thesis: NFL home underdogs of +3 to +10 are systematically undervalued on the moneyline. Books overprice road favorites due to public bias toward traveling favorites in a sport where home field advantage is worth 2.5-3 points. The consensus devig fair price on home dog ML consistently shows +EV of 3%+ compared to DraftKings posted odds. This edge is strongest in divisional games and cold-weather venues where home field is amplified.

name: nfl_late_season_eliminated_team_cover
thesis: In weeks 15-18, teams mathematically eliminated from playoff contention cover the spread at a rate exceeding the book implied probability by 4%+. Books overadjust for perceived 'motivation gap,' but NFL players play for contracts, snap bonuses, and future employment. The public bets against eliminated teams, creating inflated lines on their opponents. This effect is amplified when the eliminated team is at home and facing a playoff-clinched team that may rest starters or reduce aggressive play-calling to avoid injuries.

name: nfl_new_dc_early_season_total_mispricing
thesis: Teams that hired a new defensive coordinator see game totals systematically mispriced in weeks 1-8 because books anchor to the prior year's defensive efficiency metrics. New scheme installation creates variance: aggressive DCs replacing conservative ones see overs hit at 56%+ and vice versa. By identifying the schematic shift direction (blitz rate delta, coverage shell change) and comparing to the book's implied total, edges of 3-5% emerge before books recalibrate by mid-season.

name: nfl_post_blowout_spread_regression
thesis: Teams coming off a 20+ point victory see an inflated spread the following week as books and public overweight the dominant performance. The winning team's spread is set 1-2 points too favorable, creating value on the opponent. Conversely, teams coming off a 20+ point loss see deflated lines that overcorrect for the blowout. Mean reversion in NFL game quality is strong week-to-week — a single dominant or disastrous performance is largely noise. Consensus devig on the post-blowout opponent's side shows 3%+ edge.

name: nfl_post_bye_favorite_fade
thesis: Teams returning from a bye week as home favorites of 6+ points fail to cover the spread at a higher rate than implied. The public overvalues rest and preparation advantages, inflating the line. Opponents scheme specifically for post-bye teams using extra film study of tendencies, and the favored team faces a motivation gap against a desperate opponent.

name: nfl_post_bye_favorite_overpriced_ats
thesis: Teams returning from a bye week as home favorites of 6+ points fail to cover at a higher rate than implied. The market systematically overprices the bye-week rest and preparation advantage for already-favored teams, inflating the spread beyond true edge. The opponent, playing with desperation and no expectation, keeps games closer. Fade the post-bye home chalk.

name: nfl_post_bye_first_half_over
thesis: Teams coming off bye weeks score 2-4 more first-half points than their season average due to extra preparation time enabling heavily scripted opening drives. Books price full-game totals relatively efficiently post-bye but first-half lines lag. The edge is amplified when the post-bye team faces a bottom-10 defense or when the opposing team is on short rest. Target team first-half totals over.

name: nfl_post_bye_qb_passing_yards_under
thesis: Starting quarterbacks in their first game back from a bye week have passing yards props set too high. Offenses coming off bye tend to lean run-heavy in the first half (establishing tempo after the layoff), and opposing defenses also had an extra week to prepare coverage schemes. QB passing yards unders hit at 57%+ when the line is set within 10 yards of the QB's season average, as books don't discount the bye-week run lean.

name: nfl_post_international_game_letdown_spread
thesis: Teams returning from international games (London, Munich, Brazil series) underperform the spread by 1.5-3 points in their next domestic game due to travel fatigue, disrupted preparation schedules, and occasionally a forced bye-week timing mismatch. Books partially adjust but under-correct, especially when the returning team is favored at home. The effect compounds when the international game was played on a non-standard surface or involved 5+ timezone crossing.

name: nfl_primetime_public_fade_h2h
thesis: In primetime games (SNF, MNF, TNF) where one team receives 75%+ of public moneyline bets but the line hasn't moved toward that team (or has moved away), the contrarian side wins outright at a rate exceeding implied probability by 4-6%. Books shade primetime lines toward public perception since they know recreational volume spikes. When sharp money visibly holds the other side (evidenced by reverse line movement), the market is pricing in information the public ignores. Target moneyline on the contrarian side.

name: nfl_primetime_under_first_half
thesis: First-half unders in primetime NFL games (SNF, MNF, TNF) hit at a rate exceeding market-implied probability. Primetime games feature conservative early-game playcalling — coaches protect against early deficits on national TV, defensive coordinators dial up pressure with extra preparation time, and offenses are slower to adjust. Books price full-game totals with primetime discount but under-adjust first-half lines.

name: nfl_public_dog_reverse_steam
thesis: When an NFL underdog of +3 or more receives less than 30% of public spread bets but the line moves toward them (reverse line movement indicating sharp action), the dog covers at 57%+ rate. The divergence between public and sharp money signals mispriced underdogs.

name: nfl_public_primetime_spread_fade
thesis: In nationally televised NFL games (Sunday Night Football, Monday Night Football), public betting percentages skew 65%+ toward one side on spreads. The less-popular side covers at a rate of 53-55% ATS historically because books shade lines toward public action, creating 2-3% edge on the contrarian side. The effect is strongest when the public-side team is also a large favorite (-7 or more) in a non-divisional game, as casual bettors overweight recent narrative.

name: nfl_qb_passing_yards_weather_wind
thesis: Quarterback passing yards overs are mispriced when sustained wind exceeds 15mph in outdoor stadiums. Books adjust totals but under-correct individual QB passing props, creating systematic value on the under for passing yards in high-wind games.

name: nfl_qb_revenge_game_passing_over
thesis: Quarterback passing yard props are systematically underpriced when the QB faces a former team they played 2+ seasons with. Books price the narrative into h2h and spread markets but underadjust player props. QBs in revenge spots average 18-25 more passing yards than their season mean, driven by extended preparation, emotional motivation, and familiarity with the opposing defensive scheme. The edge is largest when the QB was released or traded rather than leaving in free agency.

name: nfl_qb_revenge_game_passing_props
thesis: Starting QBs facing their former team (traded/released within prior 2 seasons, started 8+ games for that team) exceed their passing yards prop at ~58-62% vs the implied 50%, worth 3-5% edge. Motivation and insider knowledge of defensive tendencies combine to produce above-baseline aerial output. Effect is strongest in the first revenge matchup and when the QB was released rather than traded (perceived slight).

name: nfl_qb_rushing_props_cold_weather
thesis: Dual-threat QB rushing yard props are mispriced in cold weather games (sub-35°F). Passing efficiency drops in cold/wind, leading offensive coordinators to lean on designed QB runs and RPOs. Books set QB rushing lines based on season averages without sufficient weather adjustment. Target overs on mobile QBs (season rushing avg 30+ yards) in cold-weather outdoor stadiums.

name: nfl_qb_rushing_props_cold_weather
thesis: Dual-threat QB rushing yard props are not sufficiently discounted in cold weather games (sub-35°F). Designed QB runs decrease as offensive coordinators protect QBs on frozen/slick turf, and scramble frequency drops as footing worsens. Books set rushing props off season averages without adequate weather adjustment. Unders on QB rushing yards for mobile QBs (Lamar, Josh Allen, Jalen Hurts) in cold outdoor games hit at >58%.

name: nfl_qb_rushing_props_negative_gamescript
thesis: Quarterback rushing yard props are mispriced when the projected gamescript heavily favors the opponent. Books set QB rush lines based on season averages, but QBs with rushing ability (Lamar Jackson, Jalen Hurts, Josh Allen tier) see significantly elevated rushing attempts in negative gamescript — scrambles under pressure, designed runs in catch-up mode, and garbage time. Over hits at a higher rate when the QB's team is a 6+ point underdog.

name: nfl_qb_rushing_props_negative_gamescript
thesis: Dual-threat QB rushing yard props are mispriced in games where the QB's team is a 6+ point underdog. Negative game script forces passing volume, but designed QB runs and scrambles actually increase under pressure as pocket collapses more frequently and play-action fades. Books set rushing lines assuming reduced designed runs without accounting for the scramble uptick. Overs on QB rushing yards for mobile QBs in underdog spots show persistent +EV.

name: nfl_qb_rushing_props_negative_gamescript
thesis: Quarterback rushing yard overs hit at elevated rates (~58%) when the QB's team is projected to be trailing (underdog by 3+). Books set QB rush lines based on season averages but don't adequately account for game-script-driven scrambles and designed runs in catch-up mode. Mobile QBs (top-12 in rush attempts) in underdog roles see 15-20% more rush attempts than their baseline.

name: nfl_qb_rushing_props_negative_gamescript
thesis: Quarterback rushing yard overs hit at an elevated rate when the QB's team is a 6+ point underdog. Books set QB rushing props based on season averages, but large underdogs see increased designed QB runs and scrambles in catch-up mode during the second half. Mobile QBs (top-12 in rushing attempts) in underdog spots exceed their rushing prop by 15-25% more often than the implied line suggests.

name: nfl_qb_rushing_props_negative_gamescript
thesis: Quarterback rushing yard props for mobile QBs (Lamar Jackson, Jalen Hurts, Josh Allen, Anthony Richardson tier) are set to season averages but should be adjusted by projected game script. When the QB's team is a 3+ point underdog, designed QB runs and scramble frequency increase as trailing teams lean on their most dynamic playmaker. Over on QB rushing yards hits at 58%+ in underdog spots vs 48% in favorite spots, yet books rarely adjust the line.

name: nfl_qb_windy_passing_props
thesis: Quarterback passing yard props are systematically overpriced in games with sustained winds above 15 mph. Books adjust totals for weather but underadjust individual QB passing props, creating a persistent under edge on passing yards, completions, and attempts in high-wind conditions.

name: nfl_rb_heavy_workload_regression
thesis: Running backs who received 25+ carries in their prior game see a statistically significant drop in rushing yards the following week due to accumulated fatigue, minor soft-tissue stress, and game-script regression. Books anchor RB rushing props to recent volume rather than adjusting for workload decay, creating systematic over on the posted line. Target the under on rushing yard props for RBs coming off high-volume games.

name: nfl_referee_crew_totals_bias
thesis: NFL referee crews show persistent season-over-season tendencies in penalty yards per game, with high-penalty crews inflating actual game totals by 2-4 points relative to market expectation. When a top-quartile penalty crew is assigned (typically announced Tuesday), the over on the game total is mispriced because books set lines before crew assignment and do not adjust sufficiently. The edge persists because crew assignments are public but underweighted by models.

name: nfl_revenge_game_leader_overs
thesis: Star offensive players facing their former teams within 2 seasons of departure see elevated target share, usage rate, and motivation-driven performance spikes. Books partially price the narrative but underestimate the magnitude for elite players (top-15 at position) who were traded or released rather than leaving in free agency. Player points/yards overs for these players show 4-6% edge when the consensus line is within 2 points of the player's season average.

name: nfl_revenge_game_spread_overreaction
thesis: When a team faces a former star player (traded or signed away in the prior 1-2 offseasons), public sentiment inflates the 'revenge narrative' causing the former team to be overvalued on the spread. The public bets the emotional storyline, moving the line 0.5-1.5 points past fair value. Sharp money often fades these narratives. The edge is on the side of the player's NEW team (or against the former team) when public betting percentage exceeds 60% on the former team. This is a behavioral mispricing rooted in narrative bias rather than any on-field factor.

name: nfl_revenge_qb_passing_yards_over
thesis: Starting QBs facing their former team of 2+ seasons exceed their passing yards prop at a rate above market-implied probability. Familiarity with the opposing defensive scheme and personnel packages creates a decoding advantage, while elevated motivation increases aggression. Books set props off season averages without adjusting for the schematic edge of insider knowledge.

name: nfl_road_favorite_letdown
thesis: Road favorites of 3+ points coming off a dominant win (margin 14+) underperform ATS due to motivational and preparation letdown. Books price the team's recent performance but overweight recency; the combination of road disadvantage and post-blowout complacency creates a fade opportunity on the spread.

name: nfl_short_rest_road_dog_bounce
thesis: NFL teams coming off a bye week facing opponents on short rest (Thursday-to-Sunday or Sunday-to-Thursday turnaround) cover the spread at a rate exceeding implied probability by 3-5%. Books price the bye week advantage but underweight the compounding effect of the opponent's rest disadvantage. The edge is strongest when the short-rest team also traveled 1000+ miles for the prior game.

name: nfl_short_week_away_under
thesis: Teams playing on short rest (Thursday Night Football, Monday-to-Sunday turnarounds) as the away team see compressed offensive preparation time disproportionately affecting passing game efficiency. Game totals close lower than openers 62%+ of the time in these spots, but early-week lines haven't fully adjusted. Targeting unders posted Sunday/Monday for Thursday games captures 1-3 points of closing line value before sharp money corrects by Wednesday.

name: nfl_short_week_road_dog_ats
thesis: Road underdogs playing Thursday Night Football after a previous Sunday game cover the spread at a higher rate than implied by market odds. The compressed preparation window disproportionately affects the home favorite's game-planning advantage while the public overweights home-field and recency bias on the favorite. Target road dogs getting 3+ points on short weeks.

name: nfl_short_week_road_dog_spread
thesis: Road underdogs on Thursday Night Football cover the spread at a higher rate than implied by market odds. Short preparation windows compress scheme complexity, disproportionately hurting favored teams whose game plans rely on installation depth. Books overprice the home favorite due to public bias toward the 'better' team on national TV.

name: nfl_short_week_road_dog_spread
thesis: Road underdogs on Thursday Night Football outperform the spread at a statistically significant rate. Short-week travel compounds fatigue for favorites who played a full game Sunday, while underdogs benefit from lower public expectations and inflated lines driven by recency bias on the favorite's Sunday performance. The effect is strongest when the underdog traveled fewer miles than the favorite.

name: nfl_short_week_under
thesis: Thursday Night Football and other short-rest games (fewer than 6 days between games) trend under the posted total. Physical fatigue and abbreviated game-planning reduce offensive efficiency more than books price in. The effect compounds when both teams are on short rest.

name: nfl_te_precipitation_receiving_overs
thesis: In games with measurable precipitation (rain or snow), tight end target share increases by 8-15% as QBs shift to shorter, higher-percentage routes over the middle. Books rarely adjust TE receiving yard and reception props for weather, anchoring to season averages. This creates a systematic under-pricing of TE receiving overs in precipitation games, particularly for high-usage TEs (60%+ route participation).

name: nfl_thursday_night_road_under
thesis: Thursday Night Football games where the road team traveled across at least one timezone hit the under at a rate exceeding 56%. Short rest compresses game-planning and recovery, producing conservative play-calling, higher punt rates, and lower red-zone conversion. The effect is strongest on totals set above 44.5 where the market is pricing normal offensive output despite the compressed week.

name: nfl_thursday_night_under
thesis: Thursday Night Football games go under the posted total at ~57% since 2018, driven by short-week preparation reducing offensive complexity and increasing conservative playcalling. The effect is amplified when neither team had a bye the previous week (both on true short rest). Books have partially adjusted but consensus devig still reveals 2-4% residual edge on unders in these spots.

name: nfl_thursday_night_under_short_rest
thesis: Thursday Night Football games where both teams played the previous Sunday consistently trend under the total. Short rest degrades offensive execution — route timing, protection schemes, and red zone creativity all suffer with 3 days prep. The under hits at 55%+ historically in TNF, and the edge widens when both teams rank bottom-half in offensive pace. Books have partially adjusted but still anchor totals too close to full-rest projections.

name: nfl_thursday_night_under_short_rest
thesis: Thursday Night Football games where both teams played the previous Sunday consistently go under the posted total. Short rest degrades offensive execution — route timing, pass protection communication, and red zone efficiency all decline measurably. Books have partially adjusted TNF totals downward over the years but not enough; the consensus devig still reveals under value in 55%+ of these spots. The edge is amplified when both teams rank bottom-half in offensive line continuity.

name: nfl_thursday_night_under_short_rest_both
thesis: Thursday Night Football games where both teams played the prior Sunday (not a bye) hit the under at 55-58%, representing a 3-5% edge on the total. Compressed prep cycles reduce offensive complexity and increase conservative playcalling, while fatigue amplifies defensive mistakes that lead to punts rather than scores. The effect is strongest when the game total is set ≥44.5, as books anchor to season averages and the public bets overs on primetime. Edge disappears when one team had a bye.

name: nfl_thursday_road_fatigue
thesis: Road teams playing Thursday Night Football on short rest (<=4 days) underperform the spread by 1.5-3 points due to compressed preparation and travel fatigue. Books adjust insufficiently because TNF lines open early and attract heavy public action on primetime favorites. The edge is strongest when the road team played the previous Monday or had a physical game (40+ rushing attempts allowed).

name: nfl_weather_wr_receiving_unders
thesis: Wide receiver receiving yard props are insufficiently discounted in games with wind speeds above 15 mph or precipitation probability above 60%. Books apply a small blanket reduction but don't differentiate by receiver archetype — deep-threat WRs see disproportionate target and yardage drops vs. slot receivers who run short routes. Unders on outside WRs with high average depth of target (aDOT > 12) in adverse weather represent a persistent edge.

name: nfl_west_coast_early_kickoff
thesis: West Coast teams (SEA, SF, LAR, LAC, LV, ARI) playing 1pm ET road games underperform spreads by 1-2.5 points due to circadian disadvantage (10am body clock). The effect compounds in September-October when teams haven't adapted travel routines, and is strongest for teams that didn't travel early (arrived day before). Player prop unders on passing yards and completion percentage also hit at elevated rates due to cognitive fog in early possessions.

name: nfl_west_coast_early_kickoff_dogs
thesis: West coast NFL teams (SEA, SF, LAR, LAC, LV, ARI) playing 10am local time road games on the east coast underperform their talent level due to circadian disruption. Books partially price this but the dog line moves insufficiently when combined with short weeks (Thursday/Sunday-to-Sunday). Backing east coast home teams as favorites by less than 7 yields CLV.

name: nfl_west_coast_early_kickoff_under
thesis: West Coast teams (SEA, SF, LAR, LAC, LV, ARI) playing 10am local time road games (1pm ET kickoffs) hit the under at elevated rates due to circadian disruption. name: nfl_west_coast_early_kickoff_under

name: nfl_west_coast_east_coast_early_spread

name: nfl_west_coast_team_early_kickoff_spread

Circadian disruption from the effective 10am body-clock kickoff degrades reaction time and decision-making. The effect compounds when the team played a Monday or Thursday night game the prior week, shortening recovery and amplifying the timezone shift.

name: nfl_west_east_early_kick_spread
thesis: West Coast teams (Pacific time zone) playing 1:00 PM ET road games underperform the spread. name: nfl_west_east_early_kick_spread
thesis: West Coast teams (Pacific/Mountain timezone) playing 1pm ET road games on the East Coast underperform the spread by 1.5-3 points due to circadian disadvantage (equivalent 10am local body clock). name: nfl_west_to_east_early_kick_player_passing

Books set props off season averages without adjusting for travel-direction and kickoff-time interaction. Target the under on passing yards, completions, and passing TDs in these spots.

name: nfl_wr_elevation_prop_lag
thesis: When a team's WR1 is ruled out or downgraded, books adjust the WR2/WR3 prop lines upward but not enough to reflect the full target share redistribution. Edge persists from injury announcement through game time because books anchor to season-long averages rather than immediate role change.

name: Altitude fatigue Denver visitor unders

name: Altitude fatigue second-half totals

Books price full-game totals but don't sufficiently discount visiting team fatigue compounding with altitude in the second half. name: Altitude fatigue visitor threes unders
thesis: Visiting teams playing in Denver (5,280 ft) show measurably depressed three-point shooting percentages, particularly in second halves when cardiovascular fatigue compounds. name: Altitude three-point depression visiting shooters

Books price player threes lines using season averages that don't adequately discount altitude. thesis: Visiting teams playing at high-altitude arenas (Denver, Utah) show statistically significant under-performance on player three-point props due to fatigue, altered shooting mechanics, and reduced oxygen at 5000+ feet. Effect is amplified when the visiting team played the prior night or traveled from sea-level.

name: Closing line value decay on early posted props
thesis: Player prop lines posted early (12+ hours before tip) on DraftKings carry systematically more edge than lines posted closer to game time. Capturing consensus-devig edges on props posted in the first window (overnight/early morning) and filtering for lines that haven't moved yields higher CLV at close than edges found within 3 hours of tip.

name: Closing line value momentum filter
thesis: Pre-game player prop edges identified 4-8 hours before tip that see the target book's line move toward the consensus fair value by close are confirmed sharp-validated edges with significantly higher hit rates than edges where the line stays flat or moves away. This is a meta-hypothesis: any existing prop edge signal (points, rebounds, assists, threes) that also shows 1+ point of closing line movement in the predicted direction converts at 4-6% higher rate than the same signal without CLV confirmation. Use as a second-pass filter: flag all edges at -8h, then re-check at -1h and only confirm bets where CLV is positive.

name: Closing line value momentum on early sharp moves
thesis: When a player prop line moves 0.5+ points at pinnacle/sharp books within the first 2 hours of posting but DraftKings hasn't yet adjusted, there is a 2-4 hour window where the stale DraftKings line has positive expected value in the direction of the sharp move. This isn't speed arbitrage — it exploits the systematic lag in recreational book repricing of player props specifically, where full-game lines update faster than prop markets. Track opening line timestamps and flag props where sharp consensus has moved but target book is stale.

name: Division rivalry game total unders
thesis: NBA divisional matchups (same division, 4x/season opponents) produce systematically lower-scoring games due to schematic familiarity, targeted defensive game-planning, and intensity of rivalry play. name: Early line movement CLV capture on spreads
thesis: When the NBA spread moves 1.5+ points in one direction between opening (typically 18-24hrs pre-tip) and the 6-hour-pre-tip mark, the line continues moving in the same direction 65%+ of the time through close, indicating sharp information the market hasn't fully absorbed. thesis: NBA players on games 4+ of a continuous road trip show cumulative fatigue effects on combined points+rebounds+assists that exceed the back-to-back discount books already apply. Books partially adjust for B2Bs but don't model cumulative road trip length as a separate factor. PRA unders for starters playing 30+ minutes on road trips of 4+ games carry a persistent edge.

name: Home underdog spread value
thesis: Home underdogs of 1-4 points receive insufficient home-court adjustment from books. ATS win rate exceeds implied probability by 2%+.

name: Late line movement against public totals
thesis: When the public betting percentage on a game total (over/under) exceeds 70% on one side but the line moves in the opposite direction in the final 4 hours before tip, this reverse movement signals sharp action. name: Referee crew foul rate prop mispricing
thesis: NBA referee crews have persistent, measurable foul-calling tendencies that create mispriced player points and PRA props. name: Referee foul rate prop inflation

name: Referee foul tendency player points overs

The edge compounds when the player also has a high free-throw percentage (>80%), converting the extra attempts efficiently.

name: Referee foul tendency points overs

Books price points lines off season averages without adjusting for ref crew assignment, which is typically published 1-2 hours before tip. Players who derive 25%+ of scoring from free throws see a systematic boost under high-whistle crews. Target overs when consensus devig shows 3%+ edge and the assigned crew averages 2+ fouls/48 above league mean.

name: Referee three-point foul tendency prop overs
thesis: When a referee crew's season average for three-point shooting fouls called per game is 1+ standard deviations above league mean, player three-point attempt props are underpriced because books don't adjust for crew assignment. Players who draw fouls on three-point attempts get extra free throws AND stay aggressive from deep, inflating both threes made and points. Target top-volume three-point shooters in games with foul-permissive crews.

name: Revenge game rebound prop overperformance

Books price player assist lines off season averages without adjusting for road trip length, creating value on overs for point guards in games 4+ of a road stretch.

name: Three-point specialist cold venue shooting unders

name: Usage rate spike rebounds assists unders

name: altitude_total_suppression

name: altitude_totals_denver

name: altitude_visitor_fatigue

name: altitude_visitor_second_half_totals

Target game total overs when the visiting team is arriving from a sea-level city and played the night before.

name: altitude_visitor_total_under

name: altitude_visitor_totals
